constitution.title: دستور جمهورية العراق (Constitution of the Republic of Iraq), approved by referendum on 15 October 2005, al-Waqa'i' al-Iraqiyya No. 4012 of 28 December 2005
constitution.note: Arts. 49 (one representative per 100,000 people, quota for women of at least a quarter, minorities represented), 56 (four-calendar-year term, election 45 days before it ends), 55 (speaker elected by absolute majority at the first sitting), 65 (Federation Council, to be created by law), 70 (president elected by two thirds of the Council of Representatives, else a runoff between the top two), 76 (prime minister designated and confirmed by vote), 117 and 141 (Kurdistan Region and its laws), 122 (governorates not organized in a region, with elected governorate councils), 131 and 142 (referendums). The Council of Representatives' site refuses cloud fetches with 403; the text cited is the gazetted one.

law12-2018.title: نظام توزيع المقاعد لانتخابات مجالس المحافظات غير المنتظمة بإقليم رقم (9) لسنة 2023 (seat allocation system for the governorate council elections, issued under Law No. 12 of 2018 on the elections of the Council of Representatives and governorate and district councils, as amended)
law12-2018.publisher: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
law12-2018.note: Art. 2 table: 15 governorates, 275 seats, 75 for the women's quota and 10 for components (Christians in Kirkuk, Basra, Nineveh, and Baghdad; Sabean-Mandaeans in Maysan and Baghdad; Feyli Kurds in Wasit and Baghdad; Shabak and Yazidis in Nineveh). Art. 3: list votes divided by 1.7, 3, 5, 7, 9, and so on. Scanned, no text layer.

law9-2020.title: قانون انتخابات مجلس النواب العراقي رقم (9) لسنة 2020 (Council of Representatives Elections Law No. 9 of 2020)
law9-2020.publisher: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
law9-2020.note: The law used for the 10 October 2021 election: 329 seats, multi-member districts within each governorate with single non-transferable votes for individual candidates, 9 component seats. Scanned, 18 pages.

law31-2019.title: قانون المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات رقم (31) لسنة 2019 (Independent High Electoral Commission Law No. 31 of 2019)
law31-2019.publisher: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
law31-2019.note: The commission runs federal, regional, and governorate elections and referendums across Iraq. Scanned, 13 pages.

ihec-2021-figures.title: اعداد الناخبين والمرشحين واعداد الدوائر الانتخابية وكوتا المكونات لانتخابات مجلس النواب العراقي 2021 (electors, candidates, electoral districts, and component quotas in the 2021 Council of Representatives election)
ihec-2021-figures.publisher: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
ihec-2021-figures.note: One infographic per governorate (pages 1-18) and a national page (19): 22,116,368 electors, 3,225 candidates, 83 electoral districts, 329 seats.

ihec-2018-winners.title: انتخابات مجلس النواب العراقي 2018: المرشحون الفائزون (winning candidates of the 2018 Council of Representatives election)
ihec-2018-winners.publisher: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
ihec-2018-winners.note: 329 winners with their district (the 18 governorates) and seat type (320 general, 9 component quota); no vote counts.

ihec-2025-winners.title: قائمة بالمرشحين الفائزين في انتخابات مجلس النواب العراقي 2025 (winning candidates of the 2025 Council of Representatives election)
ihec-2025-winners.publisher: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
ihec-2025-winners.note: 329 winners (320 general seats) with governorate, party number and name, candidate number, and the candidate's own votes; text layer.

ihec-gc-2023.title: النتائج النهائية لانتخابات مجالس المحافظات غير المنتظمة بإقليم 2023 المصادق عليها من قبل مجلس المفوضين: الكيانات (certified final results of the 2023 governorate council elections, by list)
ihec-gc-2023.publisher: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
ihec-gc-2023.note: One table per governorate (15) with valid votes, seats by type, and each list's votes and seats; the per-governorate candidate files are linked from https://ihec.iq/29239-2/. Scanned images.

ihec-krd-2024.title: النتائج المصادق عليها لانتخابات برلمان إقليم كوردستان العراق 2024 (certified results of the 2024 Kurdistan Region Parliament election)
ihec-krd-2024.publisher: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
ihec-krd-2024.note: Winners by governorate: Erbil 34, Sulaymaniyah 38, Duhok 25, Halabja 3 (100 seats). Per-governorate result pages are linked from https://ihec.iq/kurdistan-final-results/. Scanned images.

ihec-results.title: نتائج الانتخابات (election results index)
ihec-results.publisher: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
ihec-results.note: Links the 2018 winners PDF, the 2021 results (an embedded Power BI report at https://ihec.iq/result-2021/), the 2023 governorate council results, the 2024 Kurdistan Parliament results, and the 2025 winners. Nothing before 2018 is on the current site.

krd-parliament-history.title: History of Parliament
krd-parliament-history.note: Kurdistan Front's Law No. 1 of 1992; the election of 19 May 1992 (100 seats plus 5 Christian seats); parliaments elected in 1992, 2005, 2009, 2013, and 2018; Law No. 2 of 2009 renamed the Kurdistan National Assembly the Kurdistan Parliament and set 111 seats with 11 for Turkmen, Christian, and Armenian lists.

krd-parliament-elections.title: Elections
krd-parliament-elections.note: Partially open-list PR; elections at least every four calendar years under Art. 8 of the amended Kurdistan Election Law of 1992; last election (as the page stands) 30 September 2018.

khec.title: Independent High Commission for Elections and Referendum of the Kurdistan Region
khec.publisher: کۆمسیۆنی باڵای سەربەخۆی هەڵبژاردن و ڕاپرسی هەرێمی کوردستان (Kurdistan Region electoral commission)
khec.note: Ran the 2009, 2013, and 2018 parliament elections, the 2009 presidential election, the 2014 governorate council elections, and the 2017 referendum. Its current site has news, laws, and procedures but no result files.

counts.locator: One parliament for the region, elected in four governorate constituencies (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok, Halabja)
Pages 1-18, one per governorate; page 19 totals all governorates of Iraq
Winners listed under 18 governorates (Halabja, made the 19th governorate by a law published in May 2025, still voted within Sulaymaniyah)

classes.name: انتخابات مجلس النواب العراقي
classes.finest_note: IHEC's current site has the 2018 winners without votes, the 2021 results in an embedded Power BI report, and the 2025 winners with their own votes; polling-station results were posted for 2018 and 2021 but are not linked from the current site.
classes.note: List PR in governorate constituencies in 2005 (230 seats plus 45 national compensatory seats, 275), 2010 (325), 2014 (328), and 2018 (329); in 2021 single non-transferable votes in 83 multi-member districts (Law 9 of 2020); in 2025 open lists in the 18 governorates under Law 12 of 2018 as amended in 2023. 9 seats are reserved for Christians, Yazidis, Sabean-Mandaeans, Shabak, and Feyli Kurds, and a quarter of seats for women; the component seats are contests within this class.

cadence.administered_by: المفوضية العليا المستقلة للانتخابات (Independent High Electoral Commission)
cadence.locator: Constitution Art. 56: four calendar years from the first sitting, the election held 45 days before the term ends; Art. 64 allows early dissolution

access.evidence: 2018 winners PDF (no votes) and 2025 winners PDF with candidate votes by governorate, both with text layers
Results embedded as a Power BI report; no file download

classes.name: انتخابات الجمعية الوطنية الانتقالية
classes.locator: Elected under the Law of Administration for the State of Iraq for the Transitional Period (2004); it drafted the constitution put to referendum on 15 October 2005
classes.note: 275 seats by closed-list PR in one national constituency, elected 30 January 2005 alongside the governorate councils and the Kurdistan National Assembly; it elected the Presidency Council and drafted the constitution.
classes.disposition_reason: The commission's 2005 certified results are not on its current site (ihec.iq/results starts in 2018); copies of the earlier commission site need to be found before the national and governorate counts can be read.

classes.name: انتخابات مجالس المحافظات
classes.locator: Constitution Art. 122; Law 12 of 2018 as amended
classes.finest_note: 2023 results by list and governorate, with candidate files per governorate; scanned PDFs.
classes.note: Each governorate is one constituency. All 18 elected councils on 30 January 2005; 14 governorates outside the Kurdistan Region voted on 31 January 2009 (Kirkuk did not); 12 on 20 April 2013, with Anbar and Nineveh on 20 June 2013; Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, and Duhok on 30 April 2014 under the Kurdistan Region's commission; 15 governorates (Kirkuk included, the Kurdistan Region excluded) on 18 December 2023, after parliament suspended the councils in 2019. 2023: 275 seats, 75 women's quota seats, 10 component seats, Sainte-Lague divisors from 1.7.

access.evidence: One list-results file and one candidate file per governorate, scanned

dates.quote: توزع المقاعد على المحافظات حسب الجدول الاتي: 15 governorates, المجموع 275

classes.name: هەڵبژاردنی پەرلەمانی کوردستان
classes.finest_note: 2024 winners by governorate constituency from IHEC; the 2009-2018 results were published by the Kurdistan Region's commission and are not on its current site.
classes.note: One region-wide list-PR constituency through 2018: 105 seats in 1992 (100 plus 5 Christian), 111 from 2005 (11 for Turkmen, Christian, and Armenian lists after Law No. 2 of 2009). The 2024 election, run by the federal IHEC after a Federal Supreme Court ruling, used four governorate constituencies and 100 seats.

cadence.administered_by: Kurdistan Region electoral commission (2009-2018); Independent High Electoral Commission (2005, 2024)
cadence.locator: Art. 8 of the amended Kurdistan Election Law of 1992: elections at least every four calendar years

access.evidence: Certified winners PDF plus per-governorate result pages (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok, Halabja)
Current site has news, laws, and procedures only; no result files

dates.quote: The election, held on 19 May 1992 ... Together with the prescribed 100 seats, the first term of Parliament had 105 members.
The last election for the 111-seat legislature was held on 30 September 2018.
أسماء الفائزين لانتخابات برلمان إقليم كوردستان 2024: أربيل (34), السليمانية (38), دهوك, حلبجة (3)

classes.name: هەڵبژاردنی سەرۆکی هەرێمی کوردستان
classes.name_en: President of the Kurdistan Region, direct (leader of the liberation movement in 1992)
classes.note: On 19 May 1992 voters also chose a leader of the Kurdistan liberation movement; no candidate won a majority and the runoff was never held. The region's president was elected directly on 25 July 2009, with the parliament. Parliament chose the president in 2005 and again from 2019 (class kurdistan_president_indirect).
classes.disposition_reason: Neither the 1992 count nor the Kurdistan Region electoral commission's 2009 results are on an official site today; the commission's current site has no result files.

classes.name: انتخاب رئيس إقليم كوردستان من قبل البرلمان
classes.name_en: President of the Kurdistan Region, chosen by parliament
classes.note: The Kurdistan National Assembly chose the region's first president in June 2005; a 2019 amendment returned the choice to parliament, which elected the president on 28 May 2019.

classes.name: انتخاب رئيس الجمهورية من قبل مجلس النواب
classes.name_en: President of the Republic, chosen by the Council of Representatives
classes.locator: Constitution Art. 70: two thirds of the members in the first round, else a runoff between the top two by majority; Art. 138 (Presidency Council for the first term)
classes.note: The Transitional National Assembly chose a three-member Presidency Council on 6 April 2005, the Council of Representatives one on 22 April 2006 (Art. 138); single presidents since 2010. The prime minister is designated by the president and confirmed by a vote of confidence (Art. 76); that investiture is not an election and is not recorded.

classes.name: انتخاب رئيس مجلس النواب
classes.name_en: Speaker of the Council of Representatives
classes.locator: Constitution Art. 55: the Council elects a speaker, then a first and second deputy, by absolute majority of its members by direct secret ballot at its first sitting
classes.note: Chosen at each term's first sitting and again when the office falls vacant; the votes are recorded in the Council's minutes.

classes.name: انتخاب المحافظ من قبل مجلس المحافظة
classes.name_en: Governors, chosen by the governorate council
classes.locator: Constitution Art. 122; the councils elect the governor by absolute majority under the governorates law (Law 21 of 2008)
classes.disposition_reason: Each council records its vote in its own minutes; no commission or ministry compiles the votes, and only the winner is announced.

classes.name: الاستفتاء
classes.name_en: National referendums (including the 1995 and 2002 presidential referendums)
classes.locator: Constitution Arts. 131 and 142 (amendments by referendum); the constitution itself was approved on 15 October 2005
classes.note: The constitutional referendum of 15 October 2005 (approved; rejected by two thirds in two governorates, short of the three that would have defeated it), and the yes-or-no referendums on Saddam Hussein's presidency of 15 October 1995 and 15 October 2002. No referendum has been held under the 2005 constitution.
classes.disposition_reason: The commission's 2005 certified results by governorate are not on its current site, and the 1995 and 2002 counts exist only in the press of the time; no official canvass is reachable.

classes.name: ڕاپرسی سەربەخۆیی کوردستان
classes.note: Held on 25 September 2017 by the Kurdistan Region's commission in the region and in disputed areas outside it; the Federal Supreme Court ruled it unconstitutional on 20 November 2017.
classes.disposition_reason: The Kurdistan Region electoral commission's results are not on its current site; the federal commission did not run or publish the vote.

classes.name: انتخابات المجلس الوطني
classes.note: The Ba'ath-era National Assembly of 250 members, elected in governorate constituencies in 1980, 1984, 1989, 1996, and 2000 and dissolved in 2003.
classes.disposition_reason: No official canvass is online; the counts were printed in the government gazette and press of the time, and no copy is held by a reachable official site.

classes.name: انتخابات المجلس التشريعي لمنطقة الحكم الذاتي
classes.name_en: Legislative Council of the Kurdistan Autonomous Region (1974-1991)
classes.note: The council set up under the 1974 autonomy law was first appointed and then elected in 1980, 1986, and 1989; it lapsed when the government withdrew its administration in 1991.
classes.disposition_reason: No official canvass is online for any of the three elections.

classes.name: انتخابات مجلس النواب العراقي (العهد الملكي)
classes.name_en: Chamber of Deputies of the Kingdom of Iraq (1925-1958)
classes.note: Elected in two stages (primary electors, then deputies by liwa) under the Organic Law of 1925 until the 1952 electoral law introduced direct voting in single-member districts; about 16 elections from 1925 to 1958. The Senate was appointed by the king. The Constituent Assembly of 1924 was elected in the same two-stage way (class constituent_assembly_1924).
classes.disposition_reason: Counts were never published as an official canvass by district; the gazette printed only the winners, and no official copy is online.

dates.note: About 16 general elections, the last in May 1958

classes.name: انتخابات المجلس التأسيسي
classes.note: Chosen in two stages in 1923-1924; it ratified the Anglo-Iraqi treaty and adopted the Organic Law of 1925.
classes.disposition_reason: Only the winners were gazetted; no official canvass exists online.

classes.name: مجلس الاتحاد
classes.locator: Constitution Art. 65: a Federation Council of representatives of the regions and governorates, its formation and membership set by a law passed by two thirds of the Council of Representatives
classes.disposition_reason: The law that would create the Federation Council has never been passed, so the chamber does not exist and has never been chosen.

classes.name: مجالس الأقضية والنواحي
classes.note: Law 21 of 2008 and Law 12 of 2018 (whose title still names district councils) provided for elected qada and nahiya councils, but no such election was ever held: the councils formed in 2003-2005 by local selection sat until parliament abolished them in 2019.
classes.disposition_reason: Never elected: the councils were selected locally after 2003 and abolished in 2019 before any election was held.

classes.name: المختارون
classes.disposition_reason: Mukhtars are chosen through the governorate administration under the Mukhtars Law of 2011, not by the electoral commission, and no returns are published.

classes.name: القضاة
classes.locator: Constitution Arts. 91-92: the Higher Judicial Council nominates judges and the Federal Supreme Court is composed by law
classes.disposition_reason: No judicial or law-enforcement office in Iraq is elected; judges are appointed on the Higher Judicial Council's nomination.

classes.name: الانتخابات التمهيدية
classes.disposition_reason: Parties and alliances register their lists with the commission; the state runs no nominating contest.
